Hey Alex — quick technical note on routing/pricing options that affect $/1M:

- Hosted (pay-as-you-go): simplest for pilots; list $/1M assumptions in the model are for hosted small-batch configs. No commit required; price higher but flexible.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): with a 3-12 month commit we can push unit costs down 20-45% depending on utilization and seq-length distribution. For your 200M token forecast, dedicated capacity typically gives the best unit economics.
- Hybrid: critical low-latency routes (payments flows) go to dedicated, bursts/campaigns go to hosted with fallback.

I attached a short note in the Drive folder with sample bucketed pricing (per 1M) and utilization assumptions used in the spreadsheet. Main sensitivity: average tokens per session (3k vs 1.5k) and % of tokens served from KV cache.

Happy to join the model review tomorrow.
